decision: measured the two problems on the running simulator before changing any code
why: wanted the baseline to be the real app, not my reading of the source
result: white/paper seam visible under Add property; callout shows a literal [!info] line

decision: split the work into an epic and 16 issues, ordered harness then perf then parity
why: the user asked for tasks, and perf and parity both rebuild the same 1 MB generated bundle so they cannot run at once
result: epic 2025, children 2026-2041

decision: kept working in the main checkout with a written fence around five files
why: another session started editing this checkout mid-run; the user chose speed over a worktree because apps/mobile/ios is 1.2 GB and gitignored
result: fences: properties.tsx note-ops.ts property-types.ts property-definitions.ts icon.tsx

decision: added a new painted bridge message instead of reusing the existing metrics message
why: metrics is a 200 ms trailing-edge throttle reporting settled height, so it would have overstated every number by up to 200 ms
result: open

decision: delegated issue 2026 to a subagent with the data shape decided up front
why: the number this produces judges every later unit, so the shape was not the delegate's call
result: running

decision: surveyed all 11 desktop renderers before writing any mobile one
why: wanted to know which ones depend on IPC or renderer state, because those cannot be ported at all
result: 4 of 5 inline specs turned out to be shared vanilla DOM already

decision: resized taskBlock up and toggleListItem plus the inline set down
why: taskBlock is an IPC-backed task UI, while toggle and the inline specs are already vanilla DOM in the shared package
result: task checkbox now needs a host round trip; toggle may be a direct reuse

decision: decided mobile ships no remote thumbnail for bookmark or youtube
why: desktop fetches img.youtube.com and Google favicons straight from the renderer, which leaks the user IP; mobile CSP already blocks it and we keep it
result: text-only cards; bytes go through the host if wanted later

decision: baseline captured on the simulator: navigate to painted p50 3876 ms
why: needed a real number before setting any target
result: guestReady to painted is 3390 ms of it, 87 percent

decision: my fence failed; the other session swept 9 of my files into its own commit and twice reverted in-flight edits
why: an instruction is not concurrency control, which is exactly what the principle warns about
result: code intact, history muddled; added a safety branch ref

decision: dropped issue 2029 down the order and promoted the guest-side work
why: the SQLite chain I planned to parallelise totals about 5 ms, so unblocking it buys nothing
result: reordering

decision: coverage gate landed red on 11 keys, then I flipped it to it.fails
why: a suite red for the whole epic would cost every unit in between its regression signal; conformance.ts already had the contract for this
result: suite green, 1 expected fail, gate still live

decision: emptied the backlog by hand to prove the gate turns red when parity is reached
why: otherwise the self-enforcement was a claim rather than a fact
evidence: 4 failed 1 passed with the backlog emptied, restored to 4 passed 1 expected fail
result: self-enforcement proven

decision: breakdown put 98.5 to 99.2 percent of the wait in one host-to-guest message hop
why: measured it instead of optimising the parts that looked expensive
result: docLoadSent 472ms to docLoadRecv 3730ms, flat across a 60x content range

decision: killed the shiki and virtualisation units on the evidence
why: shiki evaluates before ready and is worth about 30ms on a quarter of notes; layout moves 55ms across a 60x range
result: 2032 demoted, 2029 stays dead

decision: opened 2044 as a diagnosis-only unit with the discriminating experiment specified
why: the obvious payload theory is contradicted by the flatness, so a guess would have burned the unit
result: running

decision: ran the probe A/B on one bundle and killed my own small-message theory
why: the two earlier runs used different bundles, so probing had never been the only variable
result: tiny envelope takes 3241ms, same as a 9KB one; payload cleared

decision: found the guest JS thread is blocked, not the channel
why: a 100ms interval fired zero times in 20 waits of 3.24s, and the mark buffer has no gating that could drop them
result: root cause is a blocked thread

decision: proved it by cutting the bundle from 4480KB to 1102KB
why: single variable, same notes, throwaway probe reverted afterwards
result: navigate to painted 3806ms fell to 566ms

decision: reinstated 2032 after demoting it myself two updates earlier
why: I measured how long shiki RUNS and drew a conclusion about what its BYTES cost
result: corrected; 2032 is now the biggest win in the epic

decision: landed the mobile-only version of the shiki cut
why: the throwaway probe had changed the shared schema and would have killed desktop syntax highlighting
result: navigate to painted 3806ms to 715ms on device

decision: checked the two specs are identical before shipping, not after
why: only defaultLanguage reaches propSchema; a differing default would flip a code block's language across devices
result: byte-identical config, language.default stays javascript

decision: moved the branch into .worktrees/mobile-editor-instant-open and ran its own Metro on 8082
why: the main checkout is on mobile-note-inline-metadata under another session, and the last run lost nine files to exactly that sharing
result: worktree isolated; app pointed at 8082 via the dev-client url

decision: scripted the device run as apps/mobile/scripts/open-trace-run.sh
why: every perf claim in this epic needs a rerunnable artifact, not a remembered command
result: terminate, launch, deep link, poll the report file

decision: re-baselined on this worktree instead of quoting the 715ms from the previous session
why: different Metro, different host state; a delta across two rigs proves nothing
result: navigate to painted p50 567ms; seedResolved to docStart is 489ms of it, 86 percent

decision: hoisted the editor webview to one instance owned by the notes stack layout
why: 489ms of the 567ms open was creating a WKWebView per note, and it was flat across 20 opens so WebKit's own warm caches were already refuted
result: navigate to painted p50 567ms to 38ms

decision: proved reuse with a host-side mark rather than the headline number
why: the same diff resets the guest marks, so a suppressed mark could have faked the win; webviewMounted and guestReady are host-side and cannot be
result: one webview created for the whole run

decision: sent round two back after the device pass, not after the test run
why: typecheck, lint and 238 unit tests were all green on a build whose note body did not render at all
result: measureLayout needs an ancestor; the host is a sibling of the Stack

decision: added a revealed mark because painted stopped meaning what the reader sees
why: the hoist put an opacity gate between the guest's paint and the screen, so the headline number could have improved without the app doing so
result: painted to revealed p50 11ms; reveal is not hiding a regression

decision: kept the webview boot cost visible instead of letting it vanish
why: prewarm moves the 489ms, it does not delete it, and a report with no row for it would read as a bigger win than it is
evidence: report line: webviews built since launch 1, last load 1595 ms
result: relocated to app launch, off the interactive path

decision: moved the RN token to the guest's paper rather than flattening the guest to white
why: the seam had to go, and picking the colder of the two would have hidden it by making the editor match the chrome instead of the other way round
result: one paper from nav bar to editor; card and popover now have a real elevation step

decision: settled dark mode by removing the promise instead of adding a palette
why: the app ships exactly one theme, so cfg.theme following the device scheme was the app lying to its own editor
evidence: cfg.theme unconditional light, DarkTheme dropped from _layout
result: a dark device now gets a consistent light app, not a dark editor in white chrome

decision: made the harness wait for revealed, and the honest number got much worse
why: painted was 36ms but the reader sees nothing until the host flips opaque; measuring to painted was measuring a frame nobody was shown
result: navigate to revealed p50 519ms, and 483ms of it is a fallback timer not an animation
